answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each identity to a fresh challenge whose response requires many sequential modular squarings, with a Wesolowski proof allowing efficient verification. A clone may run a separate chain on another GPU, but cannot split one chain’s dependency sequence to finish it sooner; creating many identities therefore multiplies the work and imposes a real-time bottleneck. The spiral of challenges, not a velvet label or a prism of copied keys, anchors cost to elapsed computation.
